claim: For autumn 2027 the first admissions round opens 16 October 2026 and closes 15 January 2027, with supporting documentation due 1 February and bachelor results published 8 April. The second round runs 15 March to 15 April 2027, with the fee-exemption deadline on 23 April, supporting documents on 21 June (IB/EB students completing this spring: 5 July), results on 9 July and replies by 16 July.
excerpt: Second admissions round … 15 March 2027 Application round opens. 15 April Application deadline … 23 April Deadline to document fee exempt status. 21 June** Supporting documentation deadline. 9 July Admissions results published. 16 July Last day to reply to your offer. … ** If you're completing your upper secondary studies this spring semester in an IB/EB programme … you have until 5 July to submit documentation of your completed upper secondary studies.
interpretation: The first round carries the most English-taught programmes, but the authority's IB page tells applicants without a completed Diploma not to use it. For a May 2027 IB candidate the working deadlines are therefore the second round's: 15 April, 23 April, and IB results by 5 July.

claim: General entry to a Swedish bachelor requires completed upper secondary education, English to the level of Swedish English 6, and mathematics to the level of Swedish Mathematics 1a/1b/1c. Specific requirements are set per programme.
excerpt: To meet the general entry requirements for bachelor's studies, you must: have successfully completed your upper secondary (high school) education (post-16), and be able to demonstrate proficiency in English. The entry requirement for bachelor's studies in Sweden is to have studied the equivalent of the Swedish upper secondary course English 6/English Level 2. For applicants who received their final school grades after 31 December 2009, there is an additional mathematics requirement. […] The equivalents listed are estimates.
interpretation: The authority labels its own subject equivalences as estimates, which is unusual and worth repeating rather than smoothing over. An IB student should treat a published IB-to-Swedish subject mapping as a guide and confirm against the programme.
